title: FreeBSD: committing/diffing a layer silently skips every file when listing the SYSTEM extattr namespace returns EPERM (jail)
body:
## Summary

On FreeBSD, when the `system` extattr namespace cannot be listed (e.g. inside a jail,
where `extattr_list_*` on the system namespace returns `EPERM`), `storage`'s
`Llistxattr` returns that `EPERM` instead of ignoring it for the non-user namespace.

`archive.tarWithOptionsTo` then treats the per-file error as "skip this entry", so
**every** file is skipped and `buildah commit` / `podman commit` (and `Diff`) produce
an empty layer. The only trace is a log line; the operation otherwise "succeeds".

## Environment

- FreeBSD jail running `podman` / `buildah`.
- `go.podman.io/storage` (formerly `github.com/containers/storage`), all versions
  since FreeBSD xattr support was added.
- Reproduces via both `podman` and `buildah`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a FreeBSD host, set  `sysctl kern.chroot_allow_open_directories=2` to fix chroot issue, then create/enter a jail.
2. `buildah from <image>`, modify the container, then `buildah commit` it
   (or `podman commit` / `podman import` + commit).
3. Inspect the resulting image/layer: it is empty.

The underlying syscall behavior in the jail:

```
# lsextattr -s system /some/path
lsextattr: extattr_list_link: Operation not permitted
# lsextattr -s user /some/path
# (works)
```

## Expected

Listing xattrs should skip the `system` namespace when it returns `EPERM` (as
`golang.org/x/sys/unix` already does), and the commit should include all files,
just without system xattrs. At minimum, this should be a hard error rather than
silently producing an empty layer.

## Actual

`buildah commit` produces an empty image, with log output such as:

```
Can't add file "..." in "..." to tar: ... operation not permitted; skipping
```

## Root cause

`storage/internal/xattrs/xattrs_freebsd.go` (moved here by the recent refactor;
previously `storage/pkg/system/xattrs_freebsd.go`):

```go
var namespaceMap = map[string]int{
	"user":   unix.EXTATTR_NAMESPACE_USER,
	"system": unix.EXTATTR_NAMESPACE_SYSTEM,
}

func listxattr(...) ([]string, error) {
	attrs := []string{}
	for namespaceName, namespace := range namespaceMap {
		namespaceAttrs, err := listxattrNS(namespace, syscallName, pathInError, listOperation)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err   // <-- EPERM from the "system" namespace aborts the whole call
		}
		for _, attr := range namespaceAttrs {
			attrs = append(attrs, namespaceName+"."+attr)
		}
	}
	return attrs, nil
}
```

In a FreeBSD jail, `extattr_list_link`/`extattr_list_fd` on
`EXTATTR_NAMESPACE_SYSTEM` returns `EPERM`. `golang.org/x/sys/unix`'s aggregate
`Listxattr`/`Llistxattr`/`Flistxattr` deliberately tolerates this
(`golang.org/x/sys/unix/xattr_bsd.go`):

```go
/* Errors accessing system attrs are ignored so that
 * we can implement the Linux-like behavior of omitting errors that
 * ... */
if e != nil {
	if e == EPERM && nsid != EXTATTR_NAMESPACE_USER {
		continue
	}
	return s, e
}
```

but `storage` reimplements the namespace loop (to preserve the namespace prefix,
see golang/go#54357) and dropped that tolerance.

Propagation:

- `storage/pkg/archive/archive.go:507` `readUserXattrToTarHeader` calls
  `Handle.Listxattr()`; `EPERM` is not `ENOTSUP`/`ErrNotSupportedPlatform`, so it
  is returned as an error.
- `storage/pkg/archive/archive.go:649` `prepareAddFile` returns the error.
- `storage/pkg/archive/archive.go:1197` `tarWithOptionsTo` logs
  `Can't add file ...; skipping` and returns `nil`, so the walk continues and
  every entry ends up skipped.

## Regression

FreeBSD xattr support was added in
`containers/storage@be173a9` ("pkg/system: add xattr syscalls on FreeBSD",
2024-11-29, by kimminss0). Before that, FreeBSD used `xattrs_unsupported.go`, so
`Llistxattr` returned the "not supported" sentinel that the archive code
tolerates. That matches reports that buildah 1.38.1
(`containers/storage v1.56.1`) still worked, and anything newer does not.

The code has since been moved/refactored (storage/v1.65.0, commits 4f93478,
0d4b728, 37909b6 / #1245), but the behavior is unchanged.

## Suggested fix

In `storage/internal/xattrs/xattrs_freebsd.go`, mirror x/sys/unix and ignore
`EPERM` for non-user namespaces:

```go
for namespaceName, namespace := range namespaceMap {
	namespaceAttrs, err := listxattrNS(namespace, syscallName, pathInError, listOperation)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, unix.EPERM) && namespace != unix.EXTATTR_NAMESPACE_USER {
			continue
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	for _, attr := range namespaceAttrs {
		attrs = append(attrs, namespaceName+"."+attr)
	}
}
```

Separately, it would be worth reconsidering whether `tarWithOptionsTo` should
skip an entry on an xattr error, or fail loudly — silently dropping files is
surprising.

## Workaround

- Use buildah 1.38.1 (`containers/storage v1.56.1`) to commit.

## Related

- Downstream report with reproduction notes: b8b/libjail#4
- `containers/storage#2168` (FreeBSD xattr, unpacking direction)
- `podman-container-tools/container-libs#1245` (recent refactor of this code)

comments.body:
Thanks!

Reading the description, all of that makes sense but I can’t easily test it, so it would be better to receive a submitter-tested pull request.

FWIW we received #1151; I don’t have any context to that, perhaps it might make sense to coordinate — OTOH this is small enough that it might not be worth it.

---

> Separately, it would be worth reconsidering whether tarWithOptionsTo should skip an entry on an xattr error, or fail loudly — silently dropping files is surprising.

This can run against a concurrently-changing source directory, so _at least_ `ENOENT` should, ideally, not cause a hard failure (but then again, if we race against `addFile` later, a hard failure is ~inevitable). It’s quite likely that `prepareAddFile` should be much more precise about ignorable / non-ignorable errors.
@alegrey91 do you want to look at the `prepareAddFile` part?
